rubrics.evidence: steps/1_pep752/instruction.md:13 explicitly says upload checks return False when denied, but the reference and grader require UploadConflictError by default. The instruction names SecurityPolicy.namespaces without specifying its container type; neither the existing CPython tree nor PEP 752 supplies this new Python API contract.

UploadTests requires exceptions for four denied-upload cases despite the stated False result. PolicyTests.test_policy_validates_namespaces and probe.py:policy_validates require exactly a tuple, an unstated representation requirement.

The sole gpt-6.1-sol attempt failed only these two unclear behaviors: four exception-versus-False assertions and one list-versus-tuple assertion. Its CLI correctly reports upload conflicts and its policy enforces ownership, so the observed failure cannot be attributed to missing security logic; there is only one rollout, not a cross-model sample.

Implementing normalized ownership, bidirectional collision checks, transfers, live metadata, repository-specific policies, persistent CLI commands, offline tools, documentation, and CPython installation requires substantial implementation and integration reasoning despite the detailed API inventory.

The solver's entire /app, including its editable python executable, is transferred to the verifier, which trusts that executable for both suite execution and the probe parent. In a scratch replay changing only harness paths, an executable replacement directly forged both grading artifacts and earned reward 1 without any packagenamespaces implementation; no golden-file leak during solving was observed.

The instruction explicitly requires Grant and GrantError to be exported from the package root, but neither grading channel imports them. Removing both exports from the reference still earned reward 1 with all 450 required tests and all 39 probe checks passing.

run_script.sh:72 executes the submitted python, and test.sh:95 also uses it to execute the allegedly trusted probe parent. A scratch submission containing only a replacement executable and report-writing helper forged the JUnit successes and probe.json, obtaining 450/450 passing and reward 1 while the feature package was absent.

The recorded solution's list-valued SecurityPolicy.namespaces and False-returning upload checks are reasonable under the provided instruction, yet both are rejected. The network prohibition is also implemented as a token blacklist, which can reject a harmless comment mentioning curl rather than testing network behavior.

The recorded verifier completed in about 64 seconds without an exception, and two reference replays produced identical passing results. The suite uses local standard-library tests and fixtures, with no external service or changing external value needed during grading.

The base tree lacks the new package, helpers, documentation, and installation entries. A baseline run of the supplied new modules produced no successful tests; 108 methods ran, and setup for the two installation methods also failed.

The recorded full verification took about one minute, with the actual 504-test suite taking roughly six seconds; reference verification likewise completed within minutes. Verification is automated and CPU-only, substantially cheaper than implementing the feature.

The reference never returns False for denied authorize_upload calls, contrary to the instruction's explicit wording. Independently, its cli.__all__ declares build_parser public, but the package root does not re-export it despite the requirement to re-export every public symbol.

No oracle trial was provided, so oracle-history consistency cannot be established. Two full scratch replays of the unchanged reference each earned reward 1, passed all 450 required IDs, and passed all 39 independent probe checks.

PEP 752 concerns package repositories and installers, while CPython has no package-index service into which these helpers integrate. Adding a standalone repository simulation to the interpreter's standard library is a synthetic setting rather than the natural location for this ecosystem change.

The work draws on packaging-name normalization, namespace security, JSON Simple API compatibility, and CPython's build and installation machinery. A generalist would need to research these conventions.

The small fixtures use representative hierarchical package names, owners, grandfathered projects, and a separate repository. Their size is sufficient for deterministic semantic checks and does not eliminate the implementation challenge.

There is genuine integration work, but the observed zero reward is explained entirely by an unstated container type and contradictory error semantics. The demonstrated artifact-forgery shortcut further prevents reward from reliably measuring implementation capability.
